Then at the bottom of the page, line 24, going on to page 37, Mr. Petrusic read to you that: "There was no need to read the paragraph again." And then said: "Although, yet again, you never mentioned in this agreement that General Mladic in response to your question what would happen to them," meaning the prisoners, "made a certain movement with his hand." And then you answered: "No, I didn't." And then you were asked: "After this agreement was concluded, you spent another four days, another four interviews, with the Prosecution. That was on the 28th, 29th, and 30th of May, and 12th July. Do you remember these conversations?" And you responded: "I remember there were a lot of interviews. I can't remember every single one of them, but I did talk to the Prosecution several times." And then Mr. Petrusic made the assertion: "And in these conversations, you never mentioned a certain gesture that Mr. Mladic made with his hand with respect to what would happen to those people?" And you said you couldn't remember that. Do you remember that bit of testimony recently? Actually, whether you remember it or not, I'll just ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 1D01005. And we didn't have this in e-court, but my friends uploaded it, so they had it and we're aware of it. And the first page, please, in English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is an information report from Mr. Bruce Bursik, who was an investigator with the OTP at the time. Subject, interviews with you on the 28th, 29th, and 30th of May, 2003. The same days Mr. Petrusic put to you. The same month as your plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's go to page 7 of the English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I know you had a lot of interviews with the OTP. This might help you remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's toward the bottom of both pages on 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't want to spend a lot of time on this, but if we look at it, clearly we can see that this page is discussing the events of 13 July 1995. If we look at the fourth paragraph from the bottom in the English, third paragraph from the bottom in your language, Mr. Nikolic, speaking of 13 July 1995, I'll read it out: "Nikolic states that he was aware of the sporadic killings taking place in Konjevic Polje. "After meeting Mladic at Konjevic Polje, Nikolic states that he asked Mladic what they were going to do with all those people (referring to the prisoners). Mladic turned and gestured with his hand with a flat wave. Nikolic states that he understood this gesture to mean that the prisoners were to be killed." Now that document uploaded by the Defence which they put to you did not mention any hand gestures -- I'm sorry. Does that refresh your recollection of when you mentioned this hand gesture to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course this helps me. I've already stated that there were quite a few of those meetings and interviews, and I think one of the questions was whether I remember when it was when I mentioned it the first time. And then I said, "No, I don't remember." But I accept that Mr. Bursik was present and we discussed a lot of things. This was just a working version, an interim version of the transcript of our interview, just for the Trial Chamber's benefit. And amongst other things, I mentioned what is recorded in this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I won't seek to tender that, Your Honours, because I think I read out a sufficient portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you have read out the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's move on now to the witness statement of Mladen Blagojevic that was just put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which I think is 1D02002. If I could have that in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no loud speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me, 1D01002.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now on page 1, paragraph 1, we can see that this statement taken by Mr. Petrusic on 23rd May of this year, that it concerns Mladen Blagojevic, born 22 March 1971, in Bratunac, son of Radisav and Milosava, nee Obaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm done with that. I just wanted to establish the date of birth and the father's -- parents' names. Could I have 65 ter 28973, please. Page 1 of both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said 65 ter 28973.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now this is a verdict of the State Court in Bosnia-Herzegovina, dated 6th November 2008. And it's finding Mladen Blagojevic, born on 22nd March 1971, in Bratunac, son of Radisav and Milosava, nee Obaskic, guilty of crimes against humanity - if we go to page 2 of both versions - as a result of crimes committed him on the night of 13, 14 July, at the Vuk Karadzic school against Muslim prisoners, shooting at them with a machine-gun, in fact. If we go back to page 1, in the second paragraph where it says "Verdict," there is a line on previous convictions, which shows that this same Mladen Blagojevic was convicted for immigration fraud in the United States on 20 September 2006, sentenced to 12 months in gaol, suspended in order for his extradition to be tried in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So we can see he was convicted for seven years for crimes against humanity and he had a prior conviction for immigration fraud, which, Mr. Nikolic, for your information, is perjury, lying on his immigration forms. And what I want to ask you, just to make it a bit briefer, since it's nowhere in the statement offered by the Defence, were you aware or did you know that Mladen Blagojevic had been convicted for crimes against humanity for crimes committed against Muslims in July 1995 and that he had been convicted of perjury?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was convicted for crimes of war and I know why, obviously. But I did not know about that other thing, that he was convicted in America for perjury, as you call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this brief excerpt. It's four pages of the judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28973 receives number P1517, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1517.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- I try to find it on the record. P1517 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now let me move on, briefly, Mr. Nikolic. Just a couple of more questions. I am going to ask you a question now just about the issue of the local staff, the staff of the organisations in the enclave. On the 3rd of June, a couple of days ago in this courtroom, at T 11972, line 8, His Honour the Presiding Judge asked you in relation to the -- what happened with the local staff: "Do you know whether that happened, you referred to them leaving and ending up in different countries, did all the local staff -- were they treated in such a way they were free to go ... or were some of them treated like the other able-bodied men who were often taken and brought to various places?" And you responded that the only case you recalled that was different was that of the Nuhanovic family.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I am now going to refer to this trial, 17 July, at T 950 to 952, the testimony of Ms. Christine Schmitz of MSF.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember, just very simply, yes or no, if can, if you remember a woman from Germany named Christine Schmitz who worked for MSF in July 1995 in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. In her testimony here, she described a man who worked for MSF, a local staff member, a male, able-bodied, named Meho who chose not to go with MSF into the DutchBat compound but who went with his family to Potocari, and she described what happened to him. My question was: Do you have any information or do you know anything about a DutchBat worker named Meho being separated on 12 or 13 July in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I haven't got that information at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. In that case I will leave it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: One last point. This is from 5th of June [sic], yesterday, I think, at T 10296, line 19, to 10297, line 4, and you were asked a question about the MUP units along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, and I want to ask you another -- a follow-up. This was a question from Defence counsel. "Mr. Nikolic, do you have any knowledge about the 13 of July and who issued the order to the MUP special brigade to deploy along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road?" And your answer was: "What I know is that Borovcanin -- they issued -- they were given the order to deploy along the road by Borovcanin and chief of centre, Dragomir Vasic, I believe." And then you were asked another question about whether they had been ordered to take any prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have P00724, please. While it's coming up, just to save time I'll say this is an RS MUP special police report dated 5 September 1995. Report on the combat engagement of the special police brigade and other police forces in Operation Srebrenica 95 in the period from 11 July to 21 July 1995. Could we just go to the back, last page, please, of each version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, sir, you can see that this was signed by the commander of the MUP Specials at that time, Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now could we go to page 2 of the English and the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you remember if you've seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now if we look at 12 July 1995, just to show the date, that we're on that entry, 12 July, and go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if we could have page 3 of the -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So the part I'm interested in, in the English it's the third paragraph from the top, it states, speaking of 12 July: "I received an order from General Mladic to send half of my men and the available technical equipment to that axis so as to block the area and fight the aforementioned formation." And actually I should have read the sentence above so that it makes sense. "In the afternoon hours, we received information from state security employees that 12.000 to 15.000 able-bodied, mostly armed, Muslims were moving from Srebrenica towards Konjevic Polje, Cerska, and Tuzla." And then it discusses the order from General Mladic. So my question is simply: Did you know about or can you comment on Mr. Borovcanin's report that, in fact, he received an order from General Mladic to deploy along the road?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I can comment on this part. There is a slight disagreement, and I know exactly what Mr. Petrusic asked me yesterday. He asked me who it was who had ordered the police units to be deployed on that road, and I answered that the order had been issued to them directly by Vasic or Borosevic -- Borovcanin, who was in command. I'm bearing this in mind and I make a distinction between an order and a decision. When it comes to the decision on the unit being deployed on that road, it is a different issue. Obviously, I am aware of this information. I have read the document. I don't have any doubts about Mr. Borovcanin's statement, which means that he received his orders from the officer in charge and that was General Mladic. He was in charge of the entire operation surrounding Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, you took us to a page of yesterday's transcript. You said it was transcript 10296 and then 10297. That must be a mistake. It should be 12096 and 12097, lines are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You're absolutely correct, Your Honour. I apologise. That is what is written in my outline. I read it out wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether it's an error on your part or the transcription, most important is that it's corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And it's even not the correct day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Ah, well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yesterday was not the 5th of July. It's today --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Of June, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was the 4th of June where these pages appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I hope the quote was correct, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There are no other problems with this quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have no further redirect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Judge Fluegge has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, at the beginning of your testimony you testified about Glogova and the mass graves there, and I'm interested to know who was the body who took the initiative for this removal of the bodies? Was that anybody within the VRS or were the civilian authorities involved?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What I know and what I already said in the examination-in-chief is that the initiative was launched, the initiative to relocate the graves by representatives of the civilian authorities. I know exactly who these people are. That was the president of the Bratunac Municipality Executive Board; the president of the Bratunac municipality; and the president of the then-SDS party in Bratunac. They were those who initiated the relocation of those two graves and their transfer from the Bratunac municipality to the territory of the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that they made this proposal, they took this initiative, but the action itself was ordered by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is -- give you an affirmative answer as far as the army is concerned, that it went down that line. I received the order or, rather, my brigade did, to engage on that assignment based on a military order and that was when Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic came to the Bratunac Brigade and informed us of the decision. That's what I know. I don't know how the actual agreement went at higher levels above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I refer back to page 11966. In one of the questions there was a quote: "'We are currently engaged in tasks issued by the Army of Republika Srpska Main Staff ...'" Is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Bench has no further questions. Mr. Petrusic, has the re-examination triggered any need for further questions to the witness? It seems that Mr. Mladic would like to consult with counsel. Could you do it at such a volume that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can hear Mr. Mladic speaking from here, so that should not happen. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nikolic, who are those three people from the civilian authorities that you mentioned when you answered the Judge's question?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the municipality at the time, from whom the initiative came, is Ljubisav Simic, the president of the municipality; then Srbislav Davidovic was the president of the Executive Board; and Miroslav Deronjic was the president of the SDS Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And finally, you will agree with me that commands are not issued by gestures or by hand. They are verbally articulated?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I know how commands are issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. This then, Mr. Nikolic, concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions during a few days, all the questions that were put to you by the parties or by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return again. The witness can be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Lindsey. Ms. Lindsey, thank you for being with us and assisting the Chamber in performing its task and you're excused. One last question, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Petrusic, were you aware of the portion which was quoted by Mr. Nicholls about the witness in one of the interviews referring to a gesture made by Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone please, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know what was the translation in the transcript. My question to Mr. Nikolic was when was it that he mentioned that gesture for the first time and whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, that's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, I want an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was. I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless you bothered the witness by asking him why he had not said anything about such an important thing, and you spent quite some time on it. You suggested to him that he never had mentioned any such gesture and it was only in re-examination that the Chamber learned about what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my whole intention was to see why he did not say that while the plea agreement was being drafted. That's the essence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic, correct me when my recollection is wrong. You referred to four days of interviews, exactly the same days Mr. Nicholls was referring to, and you suggested that he had not said any word about such a gesture even in those interviews. I think you mentioned them one by one, 29th, 30th, 31st of May. And you suggested to him that he had not mention the gestures in any of those interviews, isn't it? We'll check the transcript. We'll check the transcript. But this is -- if what my recollection tells me is true, Mr. Petrusic. But I will not comment on it. We'll first check in the transcript. We'll do that perhaps during the next break and I would like you to remain in the courtroom, to be present as well after the break. Could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll not take the break yet. We'll do that at quarter past, 15 to 20 minutes after that. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We are, Mr. President. And good afternoon to you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unnecessary to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am hearing it in B/C/S. Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps unnecessary to remind you, but I still do. You are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Vanderpuye, you are touching upon a new subject. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not going to explain again to the witness who you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, very kindly, Mr. President. Good morning again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good morning, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you make it afternoon, Mr. Vanderpuye, then we are on one line again, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's been a long morning, indeed. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. You mentioned in your previous testimony on the 1st of March, 2013, at transcript pages 9418 through 9419, that one of tasks as an investigator was to assist in the preparation of certain witnesses and exhibits. And I'd like to follow-up on that today with respect to one document in particular and that's 65 ter 28975.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could just have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll have you identify it for the Chamber and then I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, I'd like to distribute hard copies of this exhibit as well once the -- once Ms. Gallagher has identified it for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document is not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did I misspeak?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Perhaps it hasn't been released. Just a moment. Sorry. It seems we have got some technical -- well, I think it's obvious we have some technical problems, Mr. President. I'm not sure how long it will take to resolve. I can proceed with the hard copy in the interim. The Defence has received it. Oh, we have it now? Okay. I apologise, Mr. President. Okay. I think we have it now. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Do you recognise what we have on the screen now, Ms. Gallagher?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you just describe what it is, just very briefly, and then I will -- I would like to publish it to the Chamber to have a hard copy of it.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you see, it's "The Bosnian Muslim Photo Identification Book." It's a book that represents the Bosnian men that were identified as missing or alive, captured from video footage of July 12th and 13th in Potocari and also near the Sandici meadow, along the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, I'd like to hand-up the hard copies of this exhibit to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I may proceed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask a couple of background questions in relation to this exhibit. First, can you tell us when you became involved in the development of this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I briefly became involved in 2007 when I was working on the Popovic trial, and then again in 2009 when I was working on the Tolimir trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to your involvement with this exhibit, can you tell us, just generally because we'll probably touch on it a little bit later, what was the objective of your assignment?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The book has remained the same since it was created in 2003. My role was to actually make sure that it was accurate as well as to update any information such as the missing men that are identified in the book as to what their status is now, are they still missing, or have they been found dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned that it was created in 2003. To your knowledge, has this book been used in other proceedings before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I believe it was created for the Blagojevic trial and it was used in the Popovic trial as well as the Tolimir trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you involved in the updating of the book in either of those trials; that is, the Popovic or Tolimir trials?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in both trials.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you could, could you just tell the Chamber, just in general terms, what the purpose of this book is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is meant to identify the men that are seen in two videos that were taken at the time of the fall of Srebrenica or shortly after on July 12th and 13th; in particular, they were men that had been separated out in Potocari that are seen on the video, and the -- the investigation team, as early as 1996, were trying to find out what happened to those men. At the same time, there is footage from July 13th, both in Potocari and near the Sandici meadow, and there are men that had been separated out as well as men that had been captured and guarded in the meadow on July 13th, and the team was trying to identify what happened to those men.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now you've indicated a number of men that are featured in this book. Can you tell us how many, for the purposes of identification, are considered in the book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are 31 men identified in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you indicated that the stills or the photographs in the book are derived from certain video footage. Have you had an opportunity to review that footage yourself?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've looked at both videos that these photographs have been captured from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do the photographs that are in the book correspond to the video footage that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now I just want to ask you just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we can go to page number 3 in e-court, it should be, to take a look at the table of contents. It should be the same, I think, in the B/C/S -- or, rather, the B/C/S is the following page. So we'll have to split the screen, if we can, with the same exhibit, and we'll see the B/C/S on page number 4. Okay. And here we can see the index or the table of contents of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you just tell us generally or walk us through what it shows.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you see, the book is basically broken up into seven sections. The bulk of the book is what's seen in part one, which is the identifications of missing men. Part two are the identifications of men that have been found alive. And then there are seven annexes. The first two annexes comprise all the statements and identifications made by family members, neighbours, friends, who actually identified the photographs and the missing men. The second annex is similar, those statements of friends, relatives, neighbours, who identify the men or the men themselves who identified the men as survivors. Annex 3 you'll see is the testimony of Pasaga Mesic, the chief of police of Tuzla, and his transcript from the Rule 61 hearing of Karadzic and Mladic in 1996. And the two annexes after that are associated with his testimony of the photos he used to show the witnesses who identified the men. And then annex six and seven are communications that the ICTY had with Bosnian authorities regarding some of the men that had been identified both in trying to locate them in order to interview the families, and the seventh annex, those actually that had been found alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now with respect to the -- your assignment to update the contents of this exhibit, can you tell the Chamber basically how you did it and what materials you relied on in order to do so?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started with the book as is -- as it was created, so the content that you see of the photographs, of the identifications. I read all of the statements that support the identifications. So the -- the annex 1 and 2, the tables that are in the book, it's a listing of all the statements of the neighbours, relatives, friends that identified the men. I read those supporting statements. Those were statements taken in 1996 in Tuzla, as well as follow-up interviews done by the ICTY and the Srebrenica team, and that was in June of 2000. So those are two separate sets of statements that I read. I also watched the videos. I looked up the photographs that were mentioned in all of the statements. In addition, I read, of course, the testimony of Pasaga Mesic and others that have testified in some form or another about this book. I also looked up the -- I verified the missing men on the ICRC missing persons list and the ICTY Srebrenica missing person list, and checked with the ICMP database to see if any of those men have been found, if the remains have been found in any of the graves. And in addition, where we did have the documents, I read the autopsy reports and looked at some of the exhumation reports and photographs of the men that had been found in graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gallagher. With respect to the Rule 61 testimony of Pasaga Mesic that we have indicated here in annex 3, can you tell us how that was or to what extent that was used by you in relation to your assignment to update the information contained in the book as to the status of the people that are identified in it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pasaga Mesic's testimony is regarding the -- these underlining statements that he had obtained during his investigation in terms of trying to identify the men. So though I read his testimony, I went directly to the statements myself, just to read them individually. So they -- they -- they correspond, it's what he had -- had used for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we'll take a look at some of those in just a little bit. Did you rely on any other information besides the ICRC, ICMP lists, for example, the autopsy reports or exhumation photographs, things of that nature, in relation to determining or confirming whether somebody was still missing or, in fact, dead?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I just mentioned, I had looked at autopsy reports, had looked at exhumation reports, had looked at exhumation photographs, in addition to all the other documents that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I saw that you are looking at the clock as I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I was indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As many others did. We'll take a break first and we'll resume at five minutes -- 25 minutes to 2.00. But could the witness first be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who is it -- will it be you, Mr. Ivetic, who will deal with the next witness -- with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This witness, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is Mr. Lukic still around, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was in the office. He was working. I don't know if he's still here or if he's working in the office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If he would still be here, the Chamber might need him immediately after the break, so that would take in 15 or 20 minutes from now. We are not certain about that yet. It depends on what we'll discuss during the break. If he would still be around, then could you ask him to still remain standby. If not, then we'll find a solution for it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Time flies. Let's resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic is not present. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleague Lukic is in the office, and due to the shortness of time, we didn't manage to get him to come to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I specifically ask you as co-counsel to pay full attention to the matter the Chamber will raise at this moment with Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Petrusic, the Chamber is concerned about what happened in cross-examination in relation to the gesture issue, if I may call it that way. But as always, most important is first to establish what happened. Therefore, I go with you through the transcript. You referred, transcript page 36, you started referring to the statements of facts, and then you said: "After this agreement was concluded, you spent another four days for interviews," and then you mentioned the dates on which these interviews were held; that is, the 28th, 29th, and 30th of May, and the 12th of July. The Chamber understands this to be a reference to the year 2003. Is that well understood by the Chamber? The documents are not evidence so we have -- is that 2003? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having established that, the witness said that there were a lot of interviews and that he talked to the Prosecution several times. Then your next question was: "And in these conversations," these were the conversations after the agreement had been concluded, "you never mentioned a certain gesture that Mr. Mladic made with his hands with respect to what would happen to those people." The Chamber cannot but conclude that you were misrepresenting what is found in the statements given on those days because we do understand that you were aware, as you told us before the break, that there was a passage in which this gesture was specifically mentioned. Is that a proper understanding of what happened? If you say it's -- this is not what I said or -- because it's translated, then please tell us and we'll verify that on the basis of -- of the audio. Was this your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection as far as the interpretation goes. The interpretation is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we establish that that is the question that you put to the witness at that point in time. The witness answered that question, saying, well, depends on if it's -- if it's not recorded, I may now have said it, but he had no clear recollection. And then you asked him to the best of his recollection: "When did you first say or made such a gesture that General Mladic allegedly made in Konjevic Polje?" The witness said: "I don't know exactly. Maybe in one of the testimonies, but I don't know precisely when." Here the witness apparently -- of my testimonies, yes. Your question then was: "Can you cite at least one reason why you failed to do that before?" The Chamber therefore has to consider what "before" means in this context, "before" meaning before even the first of any of the testimonies of the witness. Now, as far as the Chamber is aware, this witness gave his first testimony before this Tribunal in September and early October 2003. Is there any dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then also agree with me that a suggestion to the witness that he never mentioned it before the moment he suggested as perhaps the first moment he would have mentioned it, that you were aware that he had mentioned it, that is, in one of these interviews in one of those days? And that, therefore, for a second time you suggested to him that he had not said anything about this gesture where you knew that he had done so?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you allow me a few sentences in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you focus on the matters -- if you want to say anything about that -- later in the cross-examination that you referred rather to, "Why haven't you told that in all of the interviews, why have you not always said it," that is -- is well noticed by the Chamber, but that does not change the fact in any way that in the first two questions, that you clearly suggested that the witness had never said or has never referred to a gesture during these interviews and that he had never referred to such a gesture before he testified for the first time in this Tribunal. Both suggestions which are completely wrong. We noticed that in the follow-up it went slightly different. If you keep this in mind, please add anything briefly what you would like to bring to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole problem arose due to the badly phrased question, i.e., that I failed to exclude the 12th of June as one of the interview dates. My intention was to focus on the first three interviews and the failure by Mr. Nikolic to mention this in the first three interviews. Of course, the second error followed the first error, but I must say that it was never my intention to do this on purpose or to mislead the witness. I am simply trying to explain to you and to convince you that my first question was not limited to the first three days of interviews after the -- the agreement, that is the 28th, 29th, and the 30th, and after that everything tumbled down as -- as a sandcastle. I repeat that my intention with regard to Mr. Nikolic and especially towards the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution was not an ill-conceived one. The facts that you cited, there is nothing there that I can dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we briefly have a look again at 1D101 -- 10 -- I'll restart. I'll restart. I'll restart. Could we again have a look at 1D01005. The Chamber just wanted to check what the date of this document is. It is the 23rd of June, and the -- and the -- it refers to interviews held on the 28th, the 29th, and the 30th of May. And could we just go through the document. You have -- it was in your list, Mr. Petrusic. Could you tell us where the interview of the 12th of July starts?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a separate report dated the 12th of July regarding the interview that Mr. Nikolic had with Bruce Bursik, and this report refers to the first three days. And the 12th of July report follows this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in one of those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just trying to find where we see what happened on the 12th of July. You had it on our screen previously. So if you could -- then it is -- this document exclusively refers to the three interviews.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember on which page the 12th of July report, at least the report of the interview, starts, Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that after all these interviews, i.e., after the 30th of May, there is a follow-up document dated the 12th of July, and I think that it's on page 7, although I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Could we have a look at page 7 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure about the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can look at the transcript of -- yes. So in the same document, the sixth paragraph of page 7, we see that reference is made -- yes. Mr. Petrusic, is the translation into English, is that where it clearly describes the gesture. Is there any problem with that translation or is that translation not in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no dispute about the translation, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, and this is the interview of the 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: June or July?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where do we see that this is the 12th of June? Do you know the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the first page, if we go back seven pages -- at least that's the document that I had reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the -- the Chamber would like to receive a hard copy of the document -- both the document on the -- you said you were aware of that a gesture was referred to by the witness and -- Mr. Groome, we do see that Mr. Nicholls referred to a document and read part of it. That seems to be this document. So if there is any other document as a source, Mr. Petrusic, on which you relied in this context, please tell us. The Chamber, by the way, doesn't need a hard copy of this document because it's known by its 65 ter number in e-court; therefore, the Chamber can -- can further look into it. The Chamber considered it important to verify, at least, what exactly happened and what are the documents that were relied upon by the parties in this context. The Chamber will further consider the matter and has taken notice of the fact that you have said that there was no bad intention. You have explained what in your view happened. We'll further consider the matter. Having dealt with the matter, I think we could invite the witness to be escorted into courtroom. Thank you, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, you had to wait bit longer than you were expected, but that's how life sometimes is. Mr. Vanderpuye, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon again, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could have in e-court, please, 65 ter 28975, which is the -- the identification book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a lot of noise and sound. It may be a technical matter because even if everyone seems to be frozen, it still is there. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. And we'll have to go back to -- no, actually, we can go a little bit ahead. And we'll have to go to page 5, which should be the index of identified individuals. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First I just wanted to confirm with you, if I may, Ms. Gallagher, that this is the list of 31 identified individuals that you were dealing with in the preparation or updating of this material.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The second thing I wanted to ask you was, you'd indicated that you had looked at a number of documents and that included autopsy reports, photos, ICRC records, ICMP records. First, did you rely exclusively on that information or did you compare that information amongst each other to determine whether or not it was reliable?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I looked at everything in its totality in order to rely upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you find the materials in general that you relied on in terms of updating this exhibit and confirming the status of the individuals listed here, did you find the material you relied on to be reliable?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it was reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just now go to page 7 in the B/C/S -- I'm sorry, 7 in the exhibit. And that's page 2 in the B/C/S translation, which just translates the text. I'd like to start there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we can see three individuals. We can see their names so I won't read them. And we can see they have been identified in a manner -- in a number of manners. Can you just walk us through on what this shows, that is in terms of identification of these individuals, as it relates to your assignment concerning updating this information?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I see that it comes from the Petrovic footage, so I watched the -- the footage to be able to make sure that I could identify them in -- in realtime walking past. I verified that the photograph was the same photograph that was shown to the witnesses. I read the statements that you see underneath each name when it says, "Identified by his wife," "his nephew," I read all of those underlying statements. And then I searched -- I checked the ICMP missing persons list, and I checked the ICMP database to see if they turned up there. And I also looked for them in our internal database, our ZyFIND system, to see if we had any further documentation, whether there was autopsy reports or exhumation reports or photographs of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just to put this in a bit of context, you indicated that you reviewed certain video footage with respect to it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what I'd like to do in just a minute is to show the Chamber a video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could, that's 65 ter 22287. And I'd like to play just about 30 seconds or so of that footage. We'll start at the time 00:00:54 through 00:01:24 or thereabout. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Vanderpuye, is it triple 2 or double 2, 87?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have 22287, but perhaps I'm mistaken. Yup. I apologise. Yes, 22287, Your Honour. If we're queued up, we can play it, then. I'll ask you to stop at some point, Ms. Stewart, but for the moment we can get going. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I've just played and I've stopped it just briefly here at 1 minute, 12.4 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: First, can you just describe for us the context? What are we seeing here, based on your knowledge of the investigation and your experience in this case?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in Potocari and the men and women have been moved along, being ushered either to the right or to the left, to trucks or to buses, in order to be moved out of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we can -- and is this the footage, by the way, that you reviewed in relation to your assignment concerning this exhibit, the book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And at the beginning you would have seen the exact footage that lines up with the photograph that you have in the book there, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can just play this through, very quickly, through 1 minute, 24 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Here we've stopped at 1 minute, 24.3 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's a bit blurry, but can you tell us what we're seeing in this frame?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you're seeing the women that are lined up alongside the trucks. And just prior you saw it was the men walking alongside.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can just go back now to 65 ter -- just one moment, I'm sorry. If we can go back to 65 ter 28975. And we'll go back to page 7. Mr. President, I understand that the video footage that I just showed is not yet admitted in evidence. I would like to tender it in evidence. I know that it's a lot longer that what I've played, so what I would propose, at least in the interim, is to mark it for identification at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to see what total compilation finally we'll have in evidence, that's -- Madam Registrar, the portion played would receive?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number -- reserve number P1518, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart informs me that we should have a suffix A because it will be an extract of the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Therefore, one uploaded as document 2287A receives number P1518, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you a little bit about the details we see here. Here we can see identifications through OTP interviews and an identification through Pasaga Mesic Rule 61 hearing, 9 July, with respect to Ahmo Mehmedovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am not sure if we have the right page in the B/C/S on the screen because the names are different from those of the English page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Yes, the B/C/S page should be page 2. Thank you, Your Honours. Okay. I think we've got it straight now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to multiple identifications in this case, as you can see are indicated here, was there any differentiation that you made with respect to: One, the identity of the person as distinguished from what you later learned or what you later found out happened to the person, what their status was? Are these only relating to the identification of the individual or are they relating to the status of the individual?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These that you see in the book are simply about the identification of the person. In the book it does not indicate beyond whether they are missing or they're alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of your examination as to the identity of the individuals that are named in the book, did you find any discrepancies in terms of the information you found in the evidence of Pasaga Mesic versus the information you found in the statements of various individuals that also identified the same person?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For -- for the most part, no. His testimony correlates with the statements that are listed in the indexes. There were a couple of minor mistakes that were made, such as a -- in his testimony, perhaps a wrong age, or in one occasion there is one woman who is identified in the book and he had testified it was a male -- with a male's name instead. But otherwise, the information that he gave in his testimony is the same as the information that's in the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I'm looking at the clock. It's quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to conclude for the day. But before we do that, Mr. Ivetic, if you are the one who will deal with this witness, to what extent is the dispute about the identifications of persons? Not to say that -- but just whether this person shown on the video is the person as the Prosecution claims it is. Is there a dispute about those?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't think there is even a way that we could dispute a lot of the identifications, only as to where there is documentation otherwise. But it will not be -- there will not be a cross focusing on the actual -- focusing too much on the identifications of the persons as pictured, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then perhaps, Mr. Vanderpuye, and Mr. Ivetic, perhaps you could sit together, have a cup of tea or coffee, and try to find out to what extent we should use time in court on matters which are included in this material. Ms. Gallagher, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at quarter past 9.00 in this same courtroom I -- ah, yes, half past 9.00, otherwise you would have to wait for another 15 minutes in addition to what you expected. You may follow the usher. Yes, and I should -- I'm sorry, I have forgotten to instruct you, and especially since you're -- since of your job, not to speak with anyone about your testimony under the conditions as we have spelled out earlier, whether testimony already given or still to be given. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 6th of June, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
